correctness.rationale: For each n>=2, diagonalize the exact unit-path Laplacian in its normalized DCT-II basis. A shared odd factor in gcd(2j-1,n) produces a zero cosine component. A coprime odd factor permutes absolute modal cosines modulo 2n, giving squared modal product (2n)^(-(n-1)); independently the endpoint integer Krylov matrix is unit triangular, fixing Vandermonde square (2n)^(n-1). Hence every Kalman determinant is 0 or +/-1 and every full-rank matrix is unimodular. Discrete Gramians are products of Krylov matrices at H=n or D_j C_H D_j for H>=n; continuous Gramians are D_j C_T D_j with positive definite exponential kernel for T>0. Cauchy determinant cancellation gives the gamma>0 infinite-horizon spectral product. Tests use actual verify.py package in the same directory and pass exact integer/rational calculations; finite verification is not substituted for the infinite proof. No numerical conditioning assertion is made.

value.rationale: The natural D-optimal coordinate actuator problem for unit-path Laplacian dynamics has an exact exhaustive answer for every network size, gain and time horizon: phi(2n) equally optimal nodes, explicitly characterized, without Gramian computation. The stronger unimodularity implies exact reachability of every integer target in n discrete steps using integer inputs and exposes an integer-lattice structure not encoded by rank-only controllability. It distinguishes determinant objective from trace or minimum eigenvalue; the fact is motivated as an infinite-family design classification, not an arbitrary finite slice. Path adjacency and path Laplacian are distinct operators with different endpoint diagonal structure.
